extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical and quantitative researchers (and institutional nominators) applying for Burroughs Wellcome Fund Career Awards (CAMS, CASI, PATH)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for Burroughs Wellcome Fund early-career Career Awards (CAMS, CASI, PATH), describing applicant eligibility, scientific and career-evaluation factors, application components, and review processes. Targets candidates bridging advanced postdoctoral training to early faculty independence, including quantitatively trained investigators working on biological problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: research experience and career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive candidates will have at least two years of research experience and be up to two years away from becoming an independent investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to CAMS (bridges advanced postdoctoral training and the first three years of faculty service; $700,000 over 5 years) and similar early‑career timelines in other BWF programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication record and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Be a first author on at least one publication in a peer-reviewed journal; have a significant publication record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer-reviewed first-authorship is explicitly required (CAMS and CASI mention at least one first-author paper); overall publication strength is considered in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of previous research
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients evaluated based on the quality of their previous research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment likely includes rigor, novelty, productivity, and influence of prior work; used alongside publication record to judge research caliber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential impact of proposed projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients evaluated based on the potential impact of their proposed projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider how proposed work advances the field, addresses important problems, or could lead to significant scientific or clinical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall commitment to advancing medical science
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should demonstrate an overall commitment to advancing medical science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commitment may be demonstrated via research focus, career plan, prior activities, and stated goals in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary approach (encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BWF values crossing disciplinary boundaries; proposals that integrate different fields or methods are viewed favorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation potential is an evaluation factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that show potential to translate basic findings to clinical or practical applications are favored; 'support translation of basic to clinical research' is a program goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: CASI requirement: draw on quantitative background
rubrics_metrics.description: CASI proposals must draw on quantitative background and bridge quantitative methods with biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for applicants with training in physical, mathematical, computational, or engineering sciences who apply quantitative approaches to biological problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: CASI evidence of quantitative accomplishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of significant accomplishment or competence in a quantitative discipline (papers, advanced coursework, undergraduate major).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should document quantitative credentials via publications, coursework, degrees, or demonstrable technical accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation and risk
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF selects for bold, ambitious research questions and willingness to pursue high-risk/high-reward work and to develop new tools/methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages proposals that are not incremental; reviewers look for intellectual boldness and methodological innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career trajectory, mentorship, and institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear path toward independence, strong mentorship arrangement, and institutional commitment to the PI's career are important selection themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess evidence that the award will enable independence (career plan), quality of mentors and mentoring plans, and institutional support (resources, protected time, startup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program fit: topical alignment (PATH/CASI specificity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit to the specific program focus (e.g., PATH supports early-career researchers studying microbe-host interactions; CASI targets quantitatively trained investigators working in biology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment with program priorities and topical scope is required; PATH has a different mechanism but 'similar criteria'—applicants must match the stated subject area and program intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: limited submission and institutional nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is a limited submission requiring institutional nominations and pre-application screening at the home institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow institutional internal selection processes; inability to secure an institutional nomination disqualifies external submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials and supporting documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Full application includes a detailed research plan, CV, reference letters, and detailed budget justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality of the research plan, completeness and clarity of CV, strength of reference letters, and a justified budget are components used in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications undergo external expert review and consideration by the BWF Scientific Advisory Committee, with final selection by the BWF Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple review layers inform decisions; applicants should address likely reviewer concerns (scientific merit, feasibility, career impact) knowing both external experts and advisory/board members will evaluate proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goals and candidate exceptionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: BWF aims to support exceptional scientists at critical career transitions, foster independent research careers, and bridge funding gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates whose trajectory and proposal demonstrate exceptional promise and who will benefit from transitional funding to launch independent research programs.
